text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Swapo deputy secretary general John Pandeni is out of the running for the post of secretary general, to be decided at the ruling party's congress from Wednesday. President Sam Nujoma was confirmed as the party's only presidential candidate.
- The results of a study detailing the impact of a pipeline linking the Okavango River to central Namibia, will only be made public after cabinet approves the publications of the report.
- Agriculture and consumer issues will be the main points on the agenda for negotiations between South Africa and the European Union, when the next round of talks at ministerial level kicks off.
- About 8,000 members of the Kxoe tribe will be going to court over activities endangering their land.

- Power utility Nampower will in the coming years become the biggest investor in Namibia with a new investment of billions of dollars in power supply to more than 80 percent of the country's population.
- Further unemployment looms for many workers in the fishing industry at Walvis Bay because more than 80 percent of the 25,000 tonnes sardine quota has already been caught and processed.
